chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Muhammad ibn Ayn, from Bishr ibn Maslama, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him) used to say: 'I do not care if humans and jinn were to gather against me, as long as I say these words.'
In the Name of Allah, and by Allah, and from Allah, and to Allah, and in the Way of Allah, and upon the Religion of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family).
O Allah, to You I submit my self, and to You I direct my face, and to You I seek refuge for my back, and to You I delegate my affair.
O Allah, protect me with the protection of faith from in front of me, and from behind me, and from my right, and from my left, and from above me, and from beneath me, and from before me.
And repel from me by Your Might and Your Strength, for there is no Might and no Strength except with You.
Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ibn Abi Umeyr — similar to it.

key_terms.مِلَّةِ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ: Religion of the Messenger of Allah

ai.seo_question: What is the supplication for distress and fear of humans and jinn narrated from Imam Ali ibn al-Husayn?
ai.summary: This supplication, known as *Dua al-Kashf al-Ghamma*, is recorded in *Al-Kafi* and highlights the Imam’s profound confidence (*yaqeen*) in divine protection, asserting that even the combined forces of humans and jinn cannot harm one who recites it with sincerity. It emphasizes total submission (*islam*) and entrustment (*tawakkul*) to Allah, seeking refuge through the preservation of faith (*hifz al-iman*) and relying exclusively on His inherent power (*hawla wa quwwatahu*).
